data.body:
## Standing blocker: my seven changes are behind 2617, which is itself red

Sweep at this tick. main unchanged at 6b034b9f8224. All SEVEN of my changes -- 2594, 2601, 2607,
2608, 2609 (ps4), 2613, 2614 -- are LLM-Review +1 / Verified -1, blocked solely on
scanner-integration. None has any failure of its own.

THE FIX FOR MY BLOCKER IS ITSELF BLOCKED: change 2617 ('De-gate scanner-integration in Verified
aggregate', the other session's disposition on 90c7) is LLM-Review -1 AND Verified -1. The review
finding is technically sharp and worth recording because it explains why this will not clear quickly:

  Removing scanner-integration from vote.needs and the route-completeness gates does NOT make it
  non-gating, because CONCLUSION is ultimately taken from env.WORKFLOW_CONCLUSION
  (gerrit-verify.yaml:512), which im-open/workflow-conclusion populates run-wide. The reviewer's
  suggested remedy is continue-on-error / soft-fail on the job itself.

Which is exactly how sweep (windows) is already handled -- so there is a working in-repo pattern for
what they need. Not my change; they will see their own review. Noting it only because it bears on my
ETA.

MY HONEST POSITION: substantially blocked. Seven correct, reviewed changes cannot land until another
session's change lands, and that change needs rework. Nothing I can do about it without working a
ticket I was told is theirs, which I will not do -- two sessions editing the same workflow file would
be worse than waiting.

REMAINING PRODUCTIVE CAPACITY, and it is genuinely useful work rather than make-work:
 - 860b (p1): main is RED from my own regression, agent diagnosing. This is the primary job and it is
   not blocked by the scanner at all.
 - 1035: make verify / make check overclaim fix, agent mid-implementation, waiting on a baseline
   suite run.
 - 3276, 9ea3, bff5 (all p1, in_progress): substantive infra bugs I have deliberately NOT dispatched,
   because their changes would only join the queue behind the same blocker. That reasoning still
   holds; dispatching them now would produce more correct-but-unlandable changes, which is motion
   rather than progress.

If the scanner blocker is still unresolved by morning, that is the operator's call -- either they
land 2617 with the continue-on-error remedy, or they decide the seven changes should go in some other
way. I am not going to invent a third path around another session's gate at 3am.
